scores.why: Implementability 9/10: three owners, three new files (specimen.py, destripe.py, fine.py), no edit to common.py/refine.py, fine stage = third Refiner channel copied from the vascular_refine pattern, v1 code path byte-identical when flags are off. Serial GPU time 10/10: ~2h40m including one I58 prep (45 min), two DANDI register-only regressions (40 min) and the ablations; most slack of the three. GPU memory 10/10: nothing new touches the GPU beyond a point-based Refiner at 0.3/0.15 mm (0.3 M / 2.4 M points, 3 channels) and one separable 3 mm Gaussian; the texture mask and destripe are CPU-chunked with octn already freed. Simplicity 9/10: 'remove agarose by texture, flat-field along the section axis, flip the sign and polish with masked NCC, accept only if six label-free checks pass' fits on one slide. Prior/crop path 3/10: adds nothing - no --init-transform, the whole-hemisphere search remains the only entry point, and the vascular stage still has to be switched off by hand on I58 (the 4778 s trap in v1). Engineering flaw verified in code: refine.py clamps ls/sh ABSOLUTELY (ls.clamp_(-0.15, 0.15), reg on |ls|^2 about identity), so 'Refiner.refine with the existing ls/sh clamps' is fine on I58 (structural clamp is also 0.15, vascular off) but on I46 after vascular (depth stretch 1.219, ls = 0.198) the first fine step clips the stretch - R8 will fail its +-0.03 stretch criterion unless the gate happens to reject. Not fatal because --fine is off by default on cortex, but it means the fine stage cannot be turned on generally without the 15-line fix from the accuracy design.

Implementability 5/10: four owners, seven new modules (sectioning, destripe, specimen, fine with its own dense optimiser loop, verdict, viz_fine, regress) plus edits to common.py, prep_subject.py (loader order, detector before slab normalisation), register.py (init-transform, vascular gate needing a second Refiner at T_struct, fine stage, verdict) and summarize.py - roughly 3-4x the code of the minimal design, with cross-owner coupling through prep.json keys. Not one-pass material. The slab-normalisation axis/window change (3 x period -> 99 vs legacy 100 on I46) deliberately gives up the zero-diff-by-construction property on DANDI, turning the regression from a guarantee into a measurement and forcing two re-preps (~50 min each). The section-axis detector runs on the 18.7 GB raw array at the top of the most expensive step, so a bug there costs an hour per attempt. Serial GPU time 6/10: 4.5-5.5 h mandatory (two I58 preps: 40 um smoke + native, two DANDI re-preps, ~8 register runs) plus 3 h optional; fits a long day with little slack for one failed native prep. GPU memory 8/10: dense LCC/LCC^2 on the full 11 M-voxel oct150 grid with three separable avg_pool3d passes and autograd is a few GB - safe; the 49-pose landscape self-test at 0.3 mm is trivial; CPU side (raw + octn + kd-pooled S ~ 2.3 GB f32 x2) fits the 62 GiB cgroup. Simplicity 4/10: auto-detected section axis, auto destripe by a ratio threshold, auto mask mode with a whole-hemisphere histogram signature, auto similarity selection from a 49-pose landscape, a verdict engine with ~15 flags - each is defensible, together they are hard to explain in a lab meeting and hard to debug when a flag fires. Prior path 6/10: --init-transform is added (skips search, keeps both polarities and restarts) and the vascular auto-skip from the section-phase modulation ratio is the best engineering idea of the three, but the search remains the default and the prior path is only exercised as a fallback. Good ideas, wrong dose for a one-pass v1.1.

Implementability 6/10: four owners, but the method core (specimen.py, destripe.py, fine.py, register.py wiring) is the same size as the minimal design and is cleaner in one crucial place - FineRefiner(Refiner) optimises a delta D about identity with T_start folded into loss_of, so refine.py's absolute clamps and reg become relative to the start pose with zero edits to refine.py (fixes the clamp flaw that breaks the minimal design on I46). Cost is verify.py: eight checks (restarts, LCC + Nelder-Mead MI second optimisers, inverse consistency with swapped Refiner roles, split-half, landscapes, boundary EDT per face class, known-transform recovery, three figures) owned by one agent and coupled to C through the FineLevel dataclass - that module alone is the size of the rest of v1.1 and is the part most likely not to land in one pass. One internal inconsistency to resolve before coding: LCCRefiner is declared a subclass of the point-based Refiner while the LCC is specified as separable box filters, which requires a dense grid path. Serial GPU time 8/10: ~4 h; the schedule is the smartest of the three - R0 runs the fine stage + verification on the OLD prep from the OLD pose the moment C and D land (12-18 min, earliest go/no-go, no dependency on A/B), --skip-vessels removes the 10-15 min Frangi pass and makes the vascular stage auto-off via the existing exists() check, and I46/I55 get a fine-off baseline on the current code before the fine-on comparison (correct, given the stored runs predate the code). GPU memory 8/10: default levels 0.3/0.15 mm are safe; the opt-in 0.08 mm level (octv pooled x2, 19 M points with subsample >= 2, MRI box at 0.08 mm = 83 M voxels for the cropped I58 MRI, flatten via x4-pooled low-pass) fits 24 GB on I58 and is skipped for MRI > 0.1 mm - but P2 says the signal lives at the 1.3-6 mm scale, so this level buys ~0.02 mm and should stay off by default. Simplicity 7/10: the method is as explainable as the minimal one; the verification suite is elaborate but it is exactly the 'how do we know without labels' answer the PI will ask for, and the G4 calibration on I46 (label-free U must cover the labelled residual) is the right way to make the number quotable. Prior path 7/10: --init-transform with polarity evaluated (not optimised) at the init pose, used for R0 and the R3 start-independence check; the search stays the default for the reported run, so the PI's 'prior exists' point is honoured as an option, not as the design centre.

best_ideas_to_graft: Graft onto the minimal design as the base (it is the only one that lands in one pass): (1) From ACCURACY - FineRefiner(Refiner) that optimises a delta D about identity and evaluates super().loss_of(T_start @ D): makes refine.py's absolute ls/sh clamp and |ls|^2 reg RELATIVE to the start pose with no edit to refine.py. ~15 lines, fixes the verified clamp flaw (I46 depth stretch ls = 0.198 > 0.15) and lets --fine be switched on for cortex in R8 honestly. (2) From ACCURACY/ROBUST - --init-transform PATH in register.py (skip search + structural, polarity 'auto' = evaluate both class polarities at the init pose without optimising, restarts still run). This is the position-prior path the PI described, and it enables the single best schedule trick of the three: run fine + verification on the OLD prep from the OLD pose (R0, 12-18 min) as soon as fine.py exists, before any prep lands. (3) From ACCURACY - --skip-vessels in prep (no Frangi: -10-15 min on I58, and the existing `vasc = ... exists()` check turns the vascular stage off automatically, removing the manual --vascular off trap that cost 4778 s in v1) plus viz_result.py tolerating a missing octv_vessels.npy. (4) From ROBUST - the vascular acceptance gate in register.py around line 201 (accept only if vessel-channel NCC >= 0.05, structural-channel NCC drop <= 0.03 on the same Refiner, corner move <= 3 mm; else keep T_struct and log accepted=false) and, if a cheap prep statistic is wanted, the section-phase fold of the vessel density (ratio > 1.6 -> skip). One-file change; would have prevented the v1 I58 vascular disaster. (5) From ROBUST - the smoke prep from the cached 40 um octv.npy: prep_subject.py already accepts .npy input (verified, line 104), kv = 1 at 40 um and k150 = 4 reproduce the native pool-by-8 block means, so the entire v1.1 prep path (mask auto rule, destripe, oct150 provenance, prep.json keys) can be integration-tested in ~20 min without the 13 GB .nii.gz read. Budget the native prep once, after the smoke prep passes. (6) From ACCURACY - a standalone verify_fine.py --work --run [--T] that rebuilds the 0.15 mm level from cached arrays and writes verify.json/qc_fine.png for ANY stored pose, so the v1 novasc pose gets before/after numbers (R0b) and the suite can be re-run without registering; keep the suite to restarts + LCC/MI second-optimiser agreement + inverse consistency + 1-D landscapes + boundary EDT (drop V7 recovery and the non-rigid diagnostic from v1.1 - they measure optimiser precision, not accuracy, and add owner-D scope). (7) From ACCURACY - the G4 calibration: run the same label-free suite on I46 and require U_mm >= 0.8 x the labelled residual (corner_vs_oracle 0.35-0.48 mm) before quoting U for I58; and the MI-32 non-decrease gate item as the sign-free witness. (8) From ROBUST - the small regress.py with the tolerance table (pass/fail per criterion, non-zero exit) and the destripe axis argmin guard (skip + log when the section axis is not decisive) - both cheap and reusable. Keep from MINIMAL: v1 call order byte-identical when flags are off, texture mask computed on the ORIGINAL octv (P1's validated input), oct150 pooled from destriped octv only when k150 % kv == 0, and the three-owner file partition.
fatal_flaws: MINIMAL: no fatal flaw for the I58 deliverable, two serious ones for the method claim. (a) Verified in refine.py: ls/sh are clamped absolutely (clamp_(-0.15, 0.15)) and regularised about identity, so the planned 'Refiner.refine with the existing clamps' silently clips any start pose with |ls| > 0.15 - I46 after vascular has ls = 0.198 (depth stretch 1.219). On I58 it is harmless (structural clamp is the same 0.15, vascular off), but R8 ('--fine on' on I46) will fail its +-0.03 stretch tolerance unless the gate happens to reject, so the fine stage cannot be turned on generally. (b) Ignores the PI's 'a position prior exists' constraint entirely: no --init-transform, global search is the only entry point, and the vascular stage still depends on the operator remembering --vascular off (91% of v1's I58 wall time went into a harmful vascular stage). Also, its Refiner-channel fine stage drops the moving-tissue weight (m(T)) that P2 specified - acceptable only because m_spec is eroded 1.3 mm. ROBUST: not one flaw but a dose problem - seven new modules, four owners, edits to common.py and the prep load order, coupled through prep.json keys, is not a one-pass job for 2-3 parallel agents. Specific engineering hazards: changing oct_slab_normalize's axis/window (3 x detected period = 99 vs legacy 100 on I46) forfeits zero-diff on DANDI by construction, so the regression becomes a measurement with two ~50 min re-preps and tolerances that must absorb GPU nondeterminism plus the change; the section-axis detector runs on the 18.7 GB raw array inside the ~1 h prep step, the most expensive place to discover a bug; the 49-pose similarity self-selection and the 15-flag verdict engine are hard to explain and hard to debug when a flag fires (the PI asked for simple and effective); the prior path is still only a fallback. The design would be excellent as v1.2 after the minimal core is in. ACCURACY: no fatal flaw in the method; the risk is verify.py - eight checks, three second optimisers (LCC, Nelder-Mead MI, inverse consistency with swapped Refiner roles), split-half, boundary EDT per face class, known-transform recovery and three figures, owned by one agent and coupled to C via the FineLevel dataclass - it is the size of the rest of v1.1 and the part most likely to be half-finished at the end of the pass, while the paper sentence is licensed only when F1-F4, F6, F7 all hold. Internal inconsistency: LCCRefiner is declared a subclass of the point-based Refiner but the LCC is specified as separable box filters, which needs a dense-grid path - C must pick one before coding. V7 'known-transform recovery' and the non-rigid diagnostic measure optimiser precision on the same intensities, not accuracy, and could be misquoted; keep them out of the quoted number. The opt-in 0.08 mm level is memory-safe on I58 but P2 says the informative signal is at 1.3-6 mm, so it should stay off by default. None of the three makes the crop/prior path the DEFAULT; robust and accuracy add it as an option, minimal not at all.
